summary: Discusses using ingress traffic filtering at a provider's edge to block denial of service attacks that rely on forged source addresses. The idea is to drop packets whose source address could not come from the network they entered through. It was replaced by RFC 2827.

eli5.summary: A mail room checks that the return address on every parcel matches the sender's building. Fake return addresses are thrown out, which stops many attacks.

questions: how to stop ip source address spoofing
what is a tcp syn flood
why does ingress filtering break mobile ip
subtitle: Make provider edge routers drop packets whose source address could not have come from the network they entered through.

tldr.problem: Denial of service attacks, such as TCP SYN floods, use forged source addresses, which makes them hard to stop and hard to trace.
tldr.mechanism: Filter traffic on the ingress link from a downstream network so that only packets with source addresses inside that network's legitimately advertised prefixes are forwarded, and log what is dropped.
tldr.outcome: Spoofed floods from behind the filter become much harder and attackers easier to trace. This memo was replaced by RFC 2827.

facts.label: Filter location
facts.value: Ingress link of the router serving the downstream network

today: RFC 2267 is an Informational memo that has been obsoleted by RFC 2827, which carries the current version of this guidance.

sections.title: The Problem and the Proposal
sections.content:
This informational memo responds to denial of service (DoS) attacks that use forged source addresses. It asks all providers of Internet connectivity to filter so that traffic claiming to originate outside the prefixes legitimately advertised by a downstream network is prohibited. If an ISP aggregates routing announcements for several downstream networks, strict filtering should deny traffic claiming to come from outside those announcements.

The memo is clear about the limits. The filtering does nothing against flooding attacks that originate from valid prefixes. A side benefit is that the originator can be traced more easily, since the attacker must use a valid, reachable source address.
sections.eli5: The goal is to stop people from putting fake return addresses on their mail, and to make the real sender easy to find.

sections.title: How Spoofed Floods Work
sections.content:
In the TCP SYN flood example, an attacker inside the valid prefix 9.0.0.0/8 sends SYN packets with randomly changing source addresses, drawn from private ranges that are not in global routing tables. The target reserves resources waiting for a response, and the attacker's constantly changing addresses exhaust more of them. The SYN/ACK replies find no route.

If the attacker instead uses someone else's valid address, the target sends many SYN/ACK packets to that innocent system, which becomes a secondary victim. An administrator who filters the apparent source then denies service to legitimate end-systems and becomes an unwitting accomplice of the attacker.

The memo also mentions similar UDP and ICMP flooding attacks. It says administrators should never let UDP packets destined for diagnostic ports from outside their domain reach their systems, and should consider not forwarding directed broadcasts through border routers by default. It adds that many operating system vendors made servers tolerate very high connection attempt rates, a welcome part of the solution.
sections.eli5: A prankster mails thousands of letters with made-up return addresses. The victim replies to all of them and wastes time, and some replies land on innocent neighbors.

sections.title: The Ingress Filter
sections.content:
The memo restricts transit traffic from a downstream network to the prefixes known to be intentionally advertised. In its example the attacker lives in 9.0.0.0/8, served by ISP D. An input filter on the ingress link of the router that connects the attacker's network allows only source addresses inside that prefix and denies everything else.

Network administrators should log information on dropped packets, which gives a basis for monitoring suspicious activity.

The memo also suggests future equipment could filter automatically on remote access servers, where the only valid source address for a dialed-in user's PC is the one the ISP assigned, with an option for customers who attach a subnet. It considered checking that the return path to a source leaves through the same interface the packet arrived on, but rejected it because of the many asymmetric routes in the Internet.
sections.eli5: The guard at the door only lets out letters whose return address is inside the building, and writes down the ones he turns away.

sections.title: Liabilities and Limits
sections.content:
The filtering can break some special services. Mobile IP is specifically affected, because traffic to the mobile node is tunneled while traffic from it is not, so its packets carry source addresses that do not match the network it is attached to. The memo points to work on reverse tunnels to fix this.

Filtering also does not stop an attacker from forging another host's address inside the permitted prefix range. It does guarantee that the attack comes from within the known prefixes, so the administrator can at worst block that range until the problem is resolved.

Where DHCP or BOOTP is used, packets with source 0.0.0.0 and destination 255.255.255.255 should be allowed to reach the relay agent in routers, with the scope of directed broadcast replication controlled.
sections.eli5: The rule can annoy honest travelers whose letters legitimately come from a different address, and it cannot catch someone faking a neighbor's address in the same building.

sections.title: Recommendation and Security
sections.content:
The summary urges all service providers to filter at the periphery as soon as possible, and says providers can show their network already has ingress filtering on customer links to help locate attack sources. Corporate administrators should also filter so their networks are not the source of such problems, and doing so could block a disgruntled employee from anonymous attacks.

The security section states the memo's purpose: as more providers and administrators filter, the opportunity to use forged source addresses lessens and tracking attacks becomes simpler.
sections.eli5: If everybody checks return addresses at their own door, fake ones become rare and troublemakers are easy to find.

viz.caption: THE FILTER RULE ON THE ATTACKER'S ROUTER (FROM RFC 2267)

data.title: Ingress filter on router 2
data.code:
IF    packet's source address from within 9.0.0.0/8
THEN  forward as appropriate

IF    packet's source address is anything else
THEN  deny packet
